outcome: Chang and Sun (Graph Drawing 2024) proved Harborth's conjecture for the restricted case of 4-regular planar graphs, extending earlier partial results (diamond subgraphs, non-4-edge-connected graphs) to cover the full degree-4 class; the general conjecture for all planar graphs remains open.
summary: Harborth's conjecture (every planar graph has a straight-line drawing with all-integer edge lengths, i.e. an integral Fáry embedding) remains open in general. The one result inside the 26 Jan 2024–present window that is a genuine case of this problem, rather than a variant, is Chang and Sun, 'Harborth's Conjecture for 4-Regular Planar Graphs' (LIPIcs GD 2024, DROPS record 10.4230/LIPIcs.GD.2024.38, San Francisco State University). They prove the conjecture holds for every 4-regular planar graph (extending prior work covering only 4-regular graphs with diamond subgraphs or that are not 4-edge-connected), so the conjecture is now settled for all graphs of maximum degree ≤ 4. This restricts the territory of the original problem (a degree class), so it is classified `partial`/`confirmed`, not `progress` — a whole subclass, not merely a bound, was settled, and the direction matches what the conjecture predicts. I could not extract readable text from the PDF directly (WebFetch returned only binary/compressed stream content), so I relied on the DROPS abstract page and search-engine summaries of the paper and its GD 2024 slides page (which 404'd); no acknowledgements or methods section mentioning AI, computer search, or SAT/ILP solvers surfaced anywhere I could read, and the paper's own keywords list only 'planar graphs, straight-line embeddings, Diophantine equations' — nothing suggesting automated theorem proving. I found no evidence of any AI system's involvement in this or any other Harborth's-conjecture-specific development. Two further 2025–2026 items surfaced but are variants, not cases, of Harborth's conjecture as Wikipedia states it: (1) 'On the Harborth Conjecture. Part I' (arXiv 2607.02535, submitted 2026-06-17, revised 2026-07-13) makes progress on Kleber's conjecture, a strengthening that additionally requires integer vertex coordinates (not just integer edge lengths) — it reduces Kleber's conjecture to rational-distance statements for small polygons and proves the non-degenerate-quadrilateral case, leaving pentagons and degenerate cases for future parts; this changes the hypotheses of Harborth's stated conjecture rather than restricting it, so per §3.1 it does not count as progress on this bullet. (2) Förster, Kobourov, Miller, Zink, 'Drawing Trees and Cacti with Integer Edge Lengths on a Polynomial-Size Grid' (arXiv 2509.04168, GD 2025 poster), also targets Kleber's conjecture and, for a class (trees/cacti) where existential integral Fáry embeddings were already known, supplies constructive polynomial-grid-size algorithms — an efficiency/constructiveness improvement to an already-settled case of a different (stronger) conjecture, not a new case of Harborth's conjecture itself. No AI involvement was found in either paper either. The current live Wikipedia article on Harborth's conjecture (checked as a secondary cross-check, not as the frozen source) confirms the conjecture 'remains unsolved' in general and lists the same known partial classes (bipartite, sparse, treewidth-3, degree-4 special cases, outerplanar, series-parallel, Platonic solids) plus the Kleber variant — consistent with what I found directly.
competing_reading: One could argue the Chang-Sun 4-regular result should be scored as `progress` rather than `partial` on the theory that 'degree ≤ 4' is a narrow corner of 'all planar graphs' and doesn't meaningfully move the general conjecture. But §3.1 is explicit that a case need not be large to count as `partial`, and settling an entire degree class (closing the last gap after diamond-subgraph and non-4-edge-connected cases were already known) is a clean restriction of the stated question, not a bound — so `partial` is the better fit.
what_would_settle_it: A full proof or disproof of Harborth's conjecture for all planar graphs, or evidence that Chang and Sun (or anyone else in the window) used an AI system to help find the embedding construction or Diophantine argument, which would change ai_role from none.
